principle_text: When the persuadee acknowledges shared values but does not shift toward the donation topic, avoid making only general statements without connecting to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee acknowledges the importance of donating money and time, you should introduce concrete, actionable ways for them to participate in fundraising or donation activities.
When the persuadee shows casual interest or past experience with charitable activities, you should mention your own involvement and ask about their experiences to increase engagement and openness.
When the persuadee engages in casual conversation unrelated to the charity, avoid focusing on personal entertainment preferences that do not connect to the donation goal.
When the persuadee already expresses strong support for charities, avoid generic introductions of charity organizations without connecting to their specific interests or motivations.
When the persuadee shows curiosity about a charity, avoid assuming prior knowledge and instead provide clear, informative introductions to engage their interest effectively.
When the persuadee responds with casual, off-topic answers, avoid continuing small talk that does not steer the conversation toward the charitable donation goal.
When the persuadee shows only mild recognition of a charity, avoid introducing the charity abruptly without linking it to an emotional appeal or donation motivation.
When the persuadee shows familiarity but uncertainty about a charity, you should provide a clear, positive explanation of the charity’s mission to increase their favorable perception.
When the persuadee shows familiarity with a charity but remains neutral, avoid introducing the charity casually without connecting it to their values or interests to deepen engagement.
When the persuadee engages in casual conversation without showing donation interest, avoid continuing unrelated small talk that does not guide the dialogue toward the charitable goal.
When the persuadee responds with casual, unrelated topics, avoid making neutral or generic comments that do not guide the conversation toward the charitable cause or donation opportunity.

When the persuadee responds neutrally to casual conversation without showing engagement or interest, avoid continuing small talk without gradually introducing relevant information or appeals related to the donation cause.
When the persuadee shares neutral or unrelated personal updates, avoid giving only neutral acknowledgments that do not guide the conversation toward the donation topic or increase engagement.
When the persuadee responds with casual, neutral remarks that do not indicate engagement with the charitable cause, avoid making generic comments that do not connect to the donation appeal.
When the persuadee acknowledges their own comfort or minor complaints, you should introduce contrasting situations of greater need to encourage empathy and perspective-taking.
When the persuadee has not yet mentioned charitable giving, you should ask questions that prompt them to recall past donation experiences related to the cause to encourage engagement.
When the persuadee shares past charitable involvement, avoid merely acknowledging without prompting further engagement or commitment to deepen their connection to the cause.
